symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on both treatment probabilities.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Fixed known scale used for the conditional-mean interval and conditional second central moment.

symbols.name: \(\sigma\)
symbols.def: Fixed known radius for cellwise deviations from the average treatment effect, measured in units of \(M\).

symbols.name: \(c_{\epsilon}\)
symbols.def: A positive constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

symbols.name: \(C_{\epsilon}\)
symbols.def: A finite constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

symbols.name: \(j\)
symbols.def: Second generic observed-unit index, distinct from \(i\) when used in a pair kernel.

symbols.name: \(X\)
symbols.def: Pretreatment covariate used for confounding adjustment.

symbols.name: \(P_O\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)
symbols.def: Observed margin of \(P\) under the map \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\mapsto O=(X,A,Y)\).

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(n)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space
symbols.def: \(Q_P^{(n)}:=P_O^{\otimes n}\), the law under which \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent with common law \(P_O\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\)
symbols.def: Set of measurable maps from \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) into \([-M,M]\).

symbols.name: \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\)
symbols.def: Estimator to be constructed from \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}handle}\) in \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\).

symbols.name: \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\)
symbols.def: Estimator to be constructed from \(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) in \(\mathrm{oeq:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\)
symbols.def: Selector map constructed in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) from \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\).

symbols.name: \(m\)
symbols.def: Number of observations in a generic independent block used by a factorial-moment statistic.

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(m)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(m\)-fold observed-data space
symbols.def: \(Q_P^{(m)}:=P_O^{\otimes m}\), the law of a generic block of \(m\) independent observations with common law \(P_O\).

assumptions.condition: \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

standard.name: maximal approximate effect homogeneity with outcome-scale normalization

assumptions.condition: \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^2\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

standard.name: uniform conditional second-moment and variance envelope

definitions.name: approximately homogeneous one-unit full-data law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\{P: X\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\mathbb R,\ 0<\epsilon<1/2,\ M\ge1,\ 0\le\sigma\le2,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization},\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment},\mathrm{ass:approximate\text{-}homogeneity}\}\).

definitions.name: unrestricted-heterogeneity one-unit full-data law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}:=\{P: X\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\mathbb R,\ 0<\epsilon<1/2,\ M\ge1,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization},\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\}\).

definitions.name: robust heavy-light ratio-polynomial construction handle
definitions.construction: Split the observations into two independent blocks \(I_0\) and \(I_1\).  The block \(I_0\) is used only to classify cells as heavy or light by empirical occupancy.  On light cells, use fixed shifted-Chebyshev coefficients of degree proportional to \(\log(en)\), evaluated on \(I_1\) by ordered distinct-index falling-factorial statistics carrying exactly one normalized outcome mark.  On heavy cells, use indicator-totalized arm sample-mean differences on \(I_1\), weighted by the \(I_1\) empirical cell frequency.  Sum the light and heavy contributions, multiply by \(M\), and clip to \([-M,M]\).  Set the estimator to zero outside the calibrated range.  The constants, degree, occupancy threshold, positive-denominator indicators, and fallbacks are those in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\).

definitions.name: robust collision-weighted construction handle
definitions.construction:
From \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\), \(N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k}\), \(S_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i\), \(I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\}\), and \(R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\).  Put \(\overline Y_{ak}:=S_{ak}/N_{ak}\) when \(N_{ak}>0\), and define
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{col}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left(
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
 \right),
\]
with the inner value defined to be zero when \(R_n=0\).  The map is total, measurable, and computable by one pass through the sample followed by one pass through the occupied categories.

definitions.name: known-radius total selector
definitions.construction: For \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\), let \(u_{n,d}:=d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\), \(h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+d/n^2\), and define \[\widehat\tau_n^{\star}:=\begin{cases}T_n^{\mathrm{col}},&h_{n,d,\sigma}\le\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},\\T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},&u_{n,d}<\min\{1,h_{n,d,\sigma}\},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] The displayed tie rule makes the selector a total measurable map for every \((n,d,\sigma)\).

definitions.name: radius-indexed least-favorable construction handle
definitions.construction: Begin with scaled two-point outcomes supported on \(\{-M/2,M/2\}\) and propensity values in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\). Use duality between best polynomial approximation and moment matching to choose two Poissonized priors for the marked cell intensities. Couple a common-effect coordinate with centered heterogeneous coordinates bounded by \(\sigma M\), match observable intensity moments through a degree proportional to \(\log(en)\), and transfer the separation to \(Q_P^{(n)}\). Determine the priors, degree constant, centering, normalization, and de-Poissonization in \(\mathrm{oeq:sigma\text{-}indexed\text{-}converse}\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), the causal average treatment effect is identified from \(P_O\) by \(\tau(P)=\sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k\{E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]\}\).
statements.justification: This isolates causal identification from the estimation frontier.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy use the same g-formula, so no new identification claim is made.
statements.consumer: The minimax experiment can target the observed-data functional corresponding to the 401(k) eligibility effect.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  We first verify the integrability needed below.  For every supported cell \(k\) and arm \(a\), the second-central-moment and mean-normalization assumptions give
\[
 E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]
 \le 2E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]+2\mu_{ak}^2
 \le \frac52 M^2.
\]
Hence \(E_P[|Y|\mid A=a,X=k]<\infty\).  If \(p_k>0\), overlap gives
\[
 P(A=a,X=k)=p_k\{a\pi_k+(1-a)(1-\pi_k)\}\ge p_k\epsilon>0,
\]
so both arm-specific conditional means in this cell are well defined.  Consistency implies that, on \(\{A=a\}\), \(Y=Y(a)\).  Conditional exchangeability then implies, for every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P[Y(a)\mid X=k]
 &=E_P[Y(a)\mid A=a,X=k] \\
 &=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]
 =\mu_{ak}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first equality uses conditional exchangeability and the strictly positive arm probability supplied by overlap; the second uses consistency.  The same argument applied to \(|Y(a)|\), together with the displayed second-moment bound, verifies that these potential-outcome conditional expectations are finite.

Because \(X\) has the finite support \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), the law of total expectation now yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau(P)
 &=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)] \\
 &=\sum_{k:p_k>0}p_k
 \bigl\{E_P[Y(1)\mid X=k]-E_P[Y(0)\mid X=k]\bigr\} \\
 &=\sum_{k:p_k>0}p_k
 \bigl\{E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]\bigr\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For a cell with \(p_k=0\), choose arbitrary versions of the two conditional expectations; its weighted contribution is zero.  Thus the last display equals
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k
 \bigl\{E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]\bigr\}.
\]
Finally, \(P_O\) determines every \(p_k=P_O(X=k)\) and, on every supported cell, both conditional outcome laws because overlap makes \(P_O(A=a,X=k)>0\).  It therefore determines each conditional mean in the displayed weighted sum.  The right-hand side is consequently a computable functional of \(P_O\), and it equals the causal average treatment effect by the preceding calculation. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies \(|\tau_k|\le M\), \(|\tau(P)|\le M\), and \(\max_{k:p_k>0}|\delta_k|\le2M\). Consequently \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).
statements.justification: This recomputation makes the radius normalization and unrestricted endpoint exact rather than asserted.
statements.gap: The binary normalization in Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy has the same effect range after centering; the lemma supplies the corresponding continuous-outcome normalization.
statements.consumer: The endpoint proposition and unrestricted comparator now operate on the same law class.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).  For every positive-mass cell, Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization}\) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 |\tau_k|=|\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}|
 \le |\mu_{1k}|+|\mu_{0k}|
 \le M.
\tag{1}
\]
Because the nonnegative masses sum to one, Definition~\(\mathrm{def:ate\text{-}functional}\) and (1) imply
\[
 |\tau(P)|=\left|\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\tau_k\right|
 \le \sum_{k=1}^d p_k|\tau_k|
 \le M.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus, for every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
 |\delta_k|=|\tau_k-\tau(P)|
 \le |\tau_k|+|\tau(P)|
 \le 2M.
\tag{3}
\]
Every member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) is a member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), because the former class imposes all conditions of the latter and one additional condition.  Conversely, (3) shows that every member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:approximate\text{-}homogeneity}\) at \(\sigma=2\).  The two classes are therefore equal.  Cells of zero mass play no role in any of these assertions, exactly as required by the support qualifications in the assumptions.

statements.statement: There are constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) and explicit estimators \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) supplied by Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\) such that, uniformly for \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the total selector in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) obeys \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.\] Relative to the collision guarantee in Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, Theorem 3 on page 11, the heterogeneity-dependent remainder is never larger in order and is strictly smaller when \(d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]=o(\sigma^2+d/n^2)\) and \(d=o(n\log(en))\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 L:=\log(en),\qquad
 u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2},\qquad
 h:=\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\) supplies total measurable maps \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) and, after taking the smaller dimension constant and the larger risk constant in its two displays, gives simultaneously
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min(1,u)\right\}
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+h\right)
\tag{3}
\]
throughout the stated range.  The clipping and zero fallbacks established in that theorem cover empty empirical arms, a zero collision denominator, and every boundary value of \(\sigma\).

We now inspect the three exhaustive branches of Definition~\(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\).  If
\[
 h\le\min(1,u),
\tag{4}
\]
then \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}=T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\), and (3) equals the desired bound because
\[
 \min(1,u,h)=h.
\tag{5}
\]
If
\[
 u<\min(1,h),
\tag{6}
\]
then \(u<1\), \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}=T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\), and (2) equals the desired bound because
\[
 \min(1,u,h)=u.
\tag{7}
\]
If neither (4) nor (6) holds, the tie convention in the first branch implies
\[
 1<u\quad\hbox{and}\quad 1<h,
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
 1=u<h.
\tag{8}
\]
Indeed, if \(\min(1,u)<h\) and \(u\ge\min(1,h)\), then \(u<1\) is impossible, and if \(u=1\) the strict failure of (4) gives \(h>1\).  Thus \(\min(1,u,h)=1\) in the fallback branch.  There \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}=0\), and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) yields
\[
 (\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2=\tau(P)^2
 \le M^2
 \le M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min(1,u,h)\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Combining (2)--(9), and enlarging \(C_{\epsilon}\) once, proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2
 \left\{\frac1n+\min(1,u,h)\right\}
 =C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\tag{10}
\]

For the comparison, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}collision\text{-}upper}\) records the collision remainder of order \(h\), apart from the common parametric term.  Since \(\min(1,u,h)\le h\), the selected remainder is never larger.  If \(u=o(h)\) and \(d=o(nL)\), then \(u=o(1)\), so eventually \(\min(1,u,h)=u\), and
\[
 \frac{\min(1,u,h)}{h}=\frac uh\longrightarrow0.
\tag{11}
\]
This proves the asserted strict order improvement in precisely the stated regime.  The comparison uses the published binary collision guarantee only as a benchmark; the risk bound (10) itself holds on the frozen real-outcome class under the conditional-second-moment envelope.
statements.justification: The deterministic selector converts two nonnested advantages into the upper envelope of the three-branch frontier.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, equation (12) on page 10 and Theorem 3 on page 11, give the collision branch for binary outcomes but do not hand off to the effective-sample-enlargement branch under weak moments.
statements.consumer: For \(n=9915\) and \(d=8196\), the theorem determines whether an approximate-homogeneity claim or unrestricted smoothing controls the 401(k) ATE risk.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\ge c_{\epsilon}M^2/n\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and every \(d,n\ge1\).
statements.justification: The parametric component must be supplied separately from the large-alphabet fuzzy hypotheses.
statements.gap: This is a standard two-point lower bound; the novel lower-bound content lies in the radius-indexed nonparametric term.
statements.consumer: It prevents the phase diagram from understating ordinary sampling noise in small alphabets.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(h=1/4\).  For \(v\in\{0,1\}\), construct a full-data law \(P_v\) by putting all mass on \(X=1\), drawing \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, setting \(Y(0)=0\), and setting \(Y(1)=MB_v/2\), where \(B_v\in\{-1,1\}\) and
\[
 P_v(B_v=1)=\frac12+\frac{vh}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{1}
\]
Finally set \(Y=Y(A)\).  The unused \(d-1\) cells have mass zero.  Consistency holds by construction, conditional exchangeability follows from independence of \(A\), and overlap holds because \(\pi_1=1/2\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  The conditional means are \(\mu_{01}=0\) and \(\mu_{11}=vMh/\sqrt n\), so the mean envelope holds.  Moreover \(|Y(a)-E[Y(a)\mid A=a,X=1]|\le M\), and hence the conditional second central moment is at most \(M^2\).  There is only one positive-mass cell, so \(\delta_1=0\); both laws belong to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  Their targets satisfy
\[
 \Delta_n:=|\tau(P_1)-\tau(P_0)|=\frac{Mh}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{2}
\]
Only a treated response distinguishes the two observed laws.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(Q_{P_0}^{(n)}\middle\|Q_{P_1}^{(n)}\right)
 &=-\frac n4\log\left(1-\frac{4h^2}{n}\right)\\
 &\le \frac{h^2}{1-4h^2}=\frac1{12},
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
where \(-\log(1-x)\le x/(1-x)\) for \(0\le x<1\).  Pinsker's inequality gives total variation at most \(1/\sqrt{24}<1/4\).

For any estimator \(T\), classify the law by whichever of \(\tau(P_0)\) and \(\tau(P_1)\) is closer to \(T\).  A classification error entails squared loss at least \(\Delta_n^2/4\), while the sum of the two testing errors is at least one minus total variation.  Consequently
\[
 \max_{v\in\{0,1\}}E_{Q_{P_v}^{(n)}}[(T-\tau(P_v))^2]
 \ge \frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}\left(1-\frac14\right)
 =\frac{3M^2}{512n}.
\tag{4}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(T\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) proves the lemma, for example with \(c_{\epsilon}=3/512\).  The construction is valid for every \(d,n\ge1\), including all boundary values of \(\sigma\).

statements.statement:
The two-sided bracket is matched at both required endpoints.  At \(\sigma=0\),
\[
 r_{n,d,0}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\frac d{n^2}\right\}
 \asymp n^{-1}+\frac d{n^2}
\]
uniformly for \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\).  At \(\sigma=2\),
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) and
\[
 r_{n,d,2}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
The lower expression in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) is of the same order as these two rates at \(\sigma=0\) and \(\sigma=2\), respectively.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 L:=\log(en),\qquad
 u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2},\qquad
 q:=\frac d{n^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
We may take the dimension-range constant in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) to satisfy \(c_{\epsilon}\le1\).  Thus the stipulated range implies
\[
 q\le\frac{c_{\epsilon}}L\le1.
\tag{2}
\]
For every integer \(n\ge1\), \(L^2\le4n\): indeed, \(\log n\le\sqrt n\) and \(1+\sqrt n\le2\sqrt n\).

At \(\sigma=0\), the definition of \(r_{n,d,\sigma}\) gives
\[
 r_{n,d,0}=\frac1n+\min\{1,u,q\}.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(d\ge L^2\), then \(u=q(d/L^2)\ge q\), and (2) shows that the minimum in (3) is \(q\).  If \(d<L^2\), then
\[
 q<\frac{L^2}{n^2}\le\frac4n.
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac15\left(\frac1n+q\right)
 \le \frac1n
 \le r_{n,d,0}
 \le \frac1n+q.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (3)--(5) prove uniformly that
\[
 r_{n,d,0}\asymp \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
At this endpoint the lower benchmark in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) is exactly \(n^{-1}+q\), so the bracket is order-matched.

At \(\sigma=2\), \(4+q\ge1\), and therefore
\[
 r_{n,d,2}=\frac1n+\min\{1,u\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives the support-qualified class identity
\[
 \mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}.
\tag{8}
\]
Let \(m:=\min\{1,u\}\).  The normalized lower benchmark at this endpoint is
\[
 B:=\frac1n+q+4m.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(d\ge L^2\), then \(q\le m\): when \(u\le1\), this follows from \(q\le u=m\), and when \(u>1\), it follows from (2) and \(m=1\).  Hence \(B\le5(n^{-1}+m)\).  If \(d<L^2\), (4) gives
\[
 B\le\frac5n+4m\le5\left(\frac1n+m\right).
\tag{10}
\]
Conversely, \(B\ge n^{-1}+m\).  Equations (7), (9), and (10) show
\[
 B\asymp r_{n,d,2}.
\tag{11}
\]
The common factor \(M^2\) does not affect order equivalence.  Equations (6), (8), and (11) prove both endpoint claims uniformly over the stipulated nonempty theorem range and for arbitrary zero-mass cells.  Nothing in the argument compares the benchmarks uniformly at shrinking interior radii.
statements.justification: The explicit algebra and class equality are the well-posedness sanity check for the interpolating theorem.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy establish the two binary endpoint benchmarks in Theorems 2--4; the new content is their same-class radius-indexed interpolation for real outcomes.
statements.consumer: Readers can compare the phase diagram with the two familiar benchmarks without silently changing the outcome normalization.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, uniformly over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the same model admits the radius-indexed lower bound
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
The radius-dependent family is obtained by passing the fixed-sample binary one-arm hard experiment through the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
 B\longmapsto B'\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12+\frac\sigma2\left(B-\frac12\right)\right),
 \qquad Y=M(B'-1/2).
\]
This construction has realization-wise radius at most \(\sigma M\) and preserves total-variation control by data processing.  It yields the natural product term \(\sigma^2\min\{1,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\); it does not establish the stronger interior term \(\min\{\sigma^2,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\).
statements.justification: The hypothesis-independent channel gives a rigorous same-class radius-indexed converse and exposes the product scaling forced by this contraction.
statements.gap: The construction does not supply the stronger standalone interior-radius separation requested by the original open question.
statements.consumer: It yields the honest lower side of the minimax bracket while preserving both endpoint rates.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\lambda=\sigma/2\in[0,1]\).  Start from the binary one-arm subclass in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}lower}\), with treated response \(B\in\{0,1\}\), treated cell mean \(\eta_k\in[0,1]\), and control response identically zero.  Conditional on every binary potential response \(B(a)\), independently draw
\[
 B'(a)\mid B(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
 \qquad Y(a)=M\{B'(a)-1/2\},
\tag{1}
\]
and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  The randomization in \((1)\) is independent of treatment conditional on the original potential outcomes and \(X\), so consistency and conditional exchangeability are preserved.  Propensities and cell masses are unchanged, hence overlap is preserved.

For the control and treated arms, respectively,
\[
 \mu_{0k}=-\frac{M\lambda}{2},
 \qquad
 \mu_{1k}=M\lambda(\eta_k-1/2).
\tag{2}
\]
Both means lie in \([-M/2,M/2]\).  Since \(Y(a)\in\{-M/2,M/2\}\), the absolute centered outcome is at most \(M\), so every conditional second central moment is at most \(M^2\).  Equations~\((2)\) give
\[
 \tau_k=M\lambda\eta_k,
 \qquad
 \tau(P)=M\lambda\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\eta_k.
\tag{3}
\]
Writing \(\psi:=\sum_kp_k\eta_k\),
\[
 |\tau_k-\tau(P)|=M\lambda|\eta_k-\psi|
 \le M\lambda\le\sigma M.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus every transformed law belongs to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  The verification is realization-wise, includes \(\sigma=0\), and imposes no condition on zero-mass cells.

The transformation from \((X,A,B)\) to \((X,A,Y)\) is a Markov kernel identical under the two fuzzy hypotheses.  Total variation between the induced mixtures can only decrease under this kernel.  Equivalently, for \(\lambda>0\), any estimator \(T\) in the transformed experiment can be applied after simulating \((1)\) from the source sample, and \(T/(M\lambda)\) estimates \(\psi\).  Conditional expectation given the source sample can only reduce squared loss.  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}lower}\) therefore gives, for \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n\log n\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\lambda^2
 \left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
For \(d>b_{\epsilon}n\log n\), take \(d_0=\lfloor b_{\epsilon}n\log n\rfloor\) and embed the \(d_0\)-cell construction by assigning zero mass to the remaining cells.  After decreasing the dimension constant and absorbing fixed cutoffs, \((5)\) implies
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\sigma^2
 \min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
At \(\lambda=0\), \((6)\) is the zero inequality.

Independently, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scaled\text{-}binary\text{-}exact\text{-}lower\text{-}transfer}\) yields throughout the stated range
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\tag{7}
\]
The maximum of the right sides of \((6)\) and \((7)\) is at least half their sum, which proves the displayed lower bound.  The finitely many sample sizes below the source lemmas' cutoffs are absorbed by decreasing \(c_{\epsilon}\): the displayed bracket divided by \(n^{-1}\) is uniformly bounded on the stipulated dimension and radius ranges, while Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:parametric\text{-}lower}\) supplies a fixed multiple of \(M^2/n\).

Finally, \((3)\) shows that the target separation is exactly \(M\lambda\) times the source separation.  A source separation of order \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\) becomes \(M\sigma\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\) up to constants, whose square is the product term in \((6)\).  Hence this channel proves no standalone interior separation of order \(M\min\{\sigma,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).

statements.statement:
Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\), and \(s:=\sigma^2\).  In the nonsaturated triangular regime \(L^2<d<nL\), the normalized selector and converse benchmarks
\[
 q:=\frac1n+\min\left\{u,s+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \ell:=b+su
\]
satisfy
\[
 \frac12\{b+\min(u,s)\}\le q\le b+\min(u,s),
 \qquad \ell=b+su.
\]
For every fixed \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
 \le \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
For every fixed \(C<\infty\), the same equivalence holds with constants independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) whenever at least one of
\[
 u\ge1,
 \qquad u\le Cb,
 \qquad \sigma^2\le Cb
\]
holds.  The constant-free condition \(u\le b\) is exactly
\[
 d^2\le nL^2+dL^2.
\]
In particular, \(d\le\sqrt n\,L\) is sufficient, the former small-alphabet regime \(d\le L^2\) is retained, and matching holds for every admissible alphabet whenever \(\sigma^2\le C(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\).

Consequently, along a shrinking-radius sequence, the ratio of the current upper and lower benchmarks can diverge only in the residual wedge
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad
 b\ll\sigma^2\ll1.
\]
Up to boundary constants, this is \(\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL\) together with \(\sigma^2\gg n^{-1}+d/n^2\).  The wedge is nonempty: for \(d_n=n\), \(L_n:=\log(en)\), and \(\sigma_n:=L_n^{-1/2}\), the selector benchmark divided by the proved lower benchmark satisfies
\[
 \frac{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2),\sigma_n^2+d_n/n^2\}}
 {n^{-1}+d_n/n^2+\sigma_n^2\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2)\}}
 \asymp L_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus all endpoints, every fixed interior radius, saturation, the small-alphabet regime, and both parametric-dominance elbows are matched.  Only the displayed residual wedge can require a stronger constrained converse or a sharper estimator; neither endpoint-only reasoning nor the existing radius channel decides between them.
statements.justification: This gives the strongest rate conclusion that follows from the proved same-class upper and lower bounds and localizes the unresolved part to shrinking radii.
statements.gap: The established bounds match at every fixed interior radius, but their numerical benchmarks separate along an explicit shrinking-radius sequence.
statements.consumer: A future constrained fuzzy-hypothesis or calibrated-estimator argument need only address the localized triangular regime.
statements.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 L:=\log(en),\qquad a:=\frac1n,\qquad t:=\frac d{n^2},
 \qquad b:=a+t,\qquad u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2},
 \qquad s:=\sigma^2.
\tag{1}
\]
First suppose that \(L^2<d<nL\).  Then
\[
 t<u<1,
\tag{2}
\]
because \(u/t=d/L^2>1\) and \(u=(d/(nL))^2<1\).  Hence the upper benchmark in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:frontier\text{-}upper}\) is
\[
 q=a+\min\{u,s+t\}.
\tag{3}
\]
For arbitrary nonnegative \(s,t,u\) satisfying \(t\le u\),
\[
 \frac12\{t+\min(u,s)\}
 \le \min\{u,s+t\}
 \le t+\min(u,s).
\tag{4}
\]
For the upper inequality, the middle term is at most both \(u\) and \(s+t\), and therefore at most \(t+\min(u,s)\).  For the lower inequality, if \(u\le s+t\), then its left side is at most \((t+u)/2\le u\).  If \(u>s+t\), then \(s<u\), so its left side is \((t+s)/2\le s+t\).  Adding \(a\) to (4), and using \(a\ge0\), gives
\[
 \frac12\{b+\min(u,s)\}
 \le q\le b+\min(u,s).
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(u<1\), the converse benchmark in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) is exactly
\[
 \ell=b+s\min(1,u)=b+su.
\tag{6}
\]
This proves the first part of the statement.

We next compare the theorem-level bounds over the entire stipulated dimension range.  Write
\[
 m:=\min(1,u),\qquad
 r:=a+\min\{m,s+t\},\qquad
 B:=b+sm.
\tag{7}
\]
Thus \(r=r_{n,d,\sigma}\), Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:frontier\text{-}upper}\) gives risk at most \(C_\epsilon M^2r\), and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) gives risk at least \(c_\epsilon M^2B\).

If \(\sigma\ge\underline\sigma>0\), then \(s\ge\underline\sigma^2\), whence
\[
 r\le a+m
 \le \max\{1,\underline\sigma^{-2}\}(a+sm)
 \le \max\{1,\underline\sigma^{-2}\}B.
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (8) with the two established risk bounds proves the fixed-positive-radius equivalence, after changing constants only as a function of \(\epsilon\) and \(\underline\sigma\).

The three uniform matching regimes follow from direct comparisons.  If \(u\ge1\), then \(m=1\) and
\[
 r=a+\min(1,s+t)\le a+s+t=b+s=B.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(u\le Cb\) for a fixed \(C\ge0\), then
\[
 r\le a+m\le a+u\le(1+C)b\le(1+C)B.
\tag{10}
\]
If \(s\le Cb\) for a fixed \(C\ge0\), then
\[
 r\le a+s+t=b+s\le(1+C)b\le(1+C)B.
\tag{11}
\]
For \(C<0\), the latter two conditions are impossible because \(u,b>0\) and \(s\ge0\), so the assertion, when applicable, reduces to (9).  Thus the constants in (9)--(11) are independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\), as claimed.

Multiplication by the positive number \(n^2L^2\) gives
\[
 u\le b
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 d^2\le nL^2+dL^2.
\tag{12}
\]
In particular, \(d\le\sqrt n\,L\) implies (12).  If \(d\le L^2\), then \(u=t(d/L^2)\le t\le b\), so the previously noted small-alphabet regime is included.  Equation~(11) applies for every admissible alphabet whenever \(\sigma^2=s\le Cb\).  Equations~(10) and (11) are the two parametric-dominance elbows asserted in the theorem.

It remains to localize possible divergence between the two proved benchmarks.  Suppose along a sequence that \(r/B\) is unbounded.  Equations~(9)--(11) imply that, for every fixed \(C<\infty\), eventually
\[
 u<1,qquad u>Cb,qquad s>Cb.
\tag{13}
\]
Consequently \(b=o(u)\) and \(b=o(s)\).  Equation~(8) rules out every subsequence on which \(s\) is bounded away from zero, so \(s\to0\).  It follows that \(b\to0\), and hence \(t\to0\), because \(0\le t\le b\).  If \(u\) were bounded below by some \(\eta>0\) on a further subsequence, then eventually \(s+t<u\), and (7) would yield
\[
 r=a+s+t=b+s
 \le \max\{1,\eta^{-1}\}(b+\eta s)
 \le \max\{1,\eta^{-1}\}B,
\tag{14}
\]
contradicting divergence.  Hence \(u\to0\).  We have proved that divergence can occur only when
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad b\ll s\ll1.
\tag{15}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac ub=\frac{d^2}{L^2(n+d)}.
\tag{16}
\]
Together with \(u=(d/(nL))^2\), relation (16) gives, up to boundary constants in the triangular asymptotic range, \(\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL\), while the second condition in (15) is \(\sigma^2\gg n^{-1}+d/n^2\).

Finally, the wedge is nonempty.  Take \(d_n=n\), \(L_n:=\log(en)\), and \(\sigma_n:=L_n^{-1/2}\).  Then
\[
 b_n=\frac2n,qquad u_n=\frac1{L_n^2},
 \qquad s_n=\frac1{L_n}.
\tag{17}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the numerator and denominator in the theorem's displayed ratio are, respectively,
\[
 r_n=\frac1n+\frac1{L_n^2}\asymp\frac1{L_n^2},
 \qquad
 B_n=\frac2n+\frac1{L_n^3}\asymp\frac1{L_n^3},
\tag{18}
\]
because \(L_n^3/n\to0\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac{r_n}{B_n}\asymp L_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{19}
\]
The exact-homogeneity endpoint \(s=0\) is covered by (11), every fixed positive radius, including the unrestricted endpoint \(\sigma=2\), is covered by (8), saturation is covered by (9), and the alphabet and elbow claims follow from (10)--(12).  Thus (15) is the only regime not decided by the present upper and lower bounds.  This conclusion compares proved benchmarks only and does not assert that either benchmark is the exact minimax rate inside that wedge.

The answer to the robust upper-construction question is affirmative.  For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the explicit linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) and the occupancy-weighted estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) are elements of \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\).  There are \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(n^{-1}+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
Both maps have explicit zero fallbacks and clipping, and neither bound contains an additional logarithmic factor.
statements.proof_tex:
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) constructs the explicit clipped linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,
 \frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The final clipping and the explicit zero fallback outside the calibrated range make this a measurable map into \([-M,M]\), hence \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\).

Definition~\(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) is exactly the total map denoted by \(T_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}occupancy\text{-}collision\text{-}upper}\).  That lemma gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(n^{-1}+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\tag{2}
\]
Every empirical ratio in the definition is multiplied by its positive-denominator indicator, the inner value is zero on \(R_n=0\), and the result is clipped to \([-M,M]\).  Therefore \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\).

Taking the smaller dimension constant and the larger risk constant from the two lemmas makes (1)--(2) simultaneous over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_\epsilon n^2/\log(en)\).  Both component proofs use only the stated conditional second-central-moment envelope: conditional variance controls the occupancy estimator, and the one-mark covariance calculation controls the polynomial estimator.  The endpoints \(\sigma=0,2\), empty empirical arms, and \(R_n=0\) are included, and neither display contains an additional logarithmic factor.

Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome experiment with \(p_k=1/d\), \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), conditional response means in \([0,1]\), and a common cell treatment effect, and write \(\psi(P):=d^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^d(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\).  There are constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n^2\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)}
 E_P[(\widehat\psi-\psi(P))^2]
 \ge a_{\epsilon}\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]

For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\), \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n^2\), and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge a_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Take any binary law in \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\), write its binary potential outcomes as \(B(0),B(1)\), and define
\[
 Y(a)=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y=Y(A).
\tag{1}
\]
If the source law is specified only through its observed conditional Bernoulli distributions, augment it by drawing \(B(0),B(1)\) conditionally on \(X\), independently of \(A\), with the prescribed arm means.  This gives consistency and conditional exchangeability without changing the observed experiment.  Overlap is unchanged.  Since \(Y(a)\in\{-M/2,M/2\}\), its conditional mean lies in \([-M/2,M/2]\) and its centered second moment is at most \(M^2\).  Cell effects and the ATE are multiplied by \(M\); exact homogeneity is preserved, so the resulting law belongs to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(\sigma\ge0\).

The observed transformation \(B=Y/M+1/2\) is invertible.  Consequently, every \(T\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) induces the binary estimator \(T/M\), and
\[
 E[(T-\tau(P))^2]
 =M^2E[(T/M-\psi(P^{\mathrm{bin}}))^2].
\tag{2}
\]
Restricting the supremum in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\) to these scaled laws, taking the infimum over \(T\), and applying Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}binary\text{-}exact\text{-}homogeneity\text{-}lower}\) proves the claim.

statements.statement:
Define \(N_{ak}\), \(N_k\), \(I_k\), and \(R_n\) as in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}usable\text{-}occupancy\text{-}reciprocal}\), put \(S_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i\), and set \(\overline Y_{ak}:=S_{ak}/N_{ak}\) when \(N_{ak}>0\).  The explicit total estimator
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{occ}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left(
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
 \right),
\]
with inner value zero when \(R_n=0\), satisfies, for constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{occ}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right)
\]
whenever \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\widetilde T_n\) denote the expression inside the clipping operation and let \(\mathcal G:=\sigma((X_i,A_i)_{i=1}^n)\).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives \(\tau(P)\in[-M,M]\), so projection onto this interval cannot increase squared loss.  It is enough to control \(\widetilde T_n\).

Conditional independence and the definitions of the cell means give
\[
 E[\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G]
 =\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\tau_k.
\tag{1}
\]
On \(\{R_n>0\}\), subtracting \(\tau(P)\) from \((1)\) produces a convex combination of the deviations \(\delta_k\), so approximate homogeneity bounds its absolute value by \(\sigma M\).  On \(\{R_n=0\}\), the conditional mean of the fallback is zero and \(|\tau(P)|\le M\).  Hence
\[
 E\!\left[\{E[\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G]-\tau(P)\}^2\right]
 \le M^2\{\sigma^2+Q_P^{(n)}(R_n=0)\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Write \(v_{ak}:=\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=a,X=k)\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\) gives \(v_{ak}\le M^2\).  Conditional on \(\mathcal G\), the empirical arm means use disjoint observations and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G)
 \le \frac{M^2\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n^2}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_k^2I_k\left(\frac1{N_{1k}}+\frac1{N_{0k}}\right).
\tag{3}
\]
Every denominator in \((3)\) is positive because its summand is multiplied by \(I_k\).

Conditional on the category counts, the variables \(N_{1k}\) are independent \(\operatorname{Binomial}(N_k,\pi_k)\) variables.  If \(D\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), \(m\ge2\), and \(J:=\mathbf 1\{0<D<m\}\), then
\[
 E\left[\frac1D\,\middle|\,J=1\right]
 \le \frac{2}{(m+1)q\{1-q^m-(1-q)^m\}}
 \le \frac{C_{\epsilon}}m,
\tag{4}
\]
uniformly for \(q\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  Indeed, \(D^{-1}\le2(D+1)^{-1}\) on \(D\ge1\),
\[
 E[(D+1)^{-1}]=\frac{1-(1-q)^{m+1}}{(m+1)q},
\]
and \(P(J=1)=1-q^m-(1-q)^m\ge2q(1-q)\ge2\epsilon(1-\epsilon)\).  The same calculation applies to \((m-D)^{-1}\).  Conditioning further on \((I_k)_k\) preserves independence across cells.  Since \(R_n=\sum_kN_kI_k\), equations~\((3)\)--\((4)\) yield
\[
 E[\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde T_n\mid\mathcal G)\mid(N_k,I_k)_k]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}.
\tag{5}
\]
The conditional bias--variance identity, \((2)\), \((5)\), and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:zeng\text{-}usable\text{-}occupancy\text{-}reciprocal}\) imply
\[
 E[(\widetilde T_n-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\sigma^2+\frac{n\vee d}{n^2}
 +\exp\left(-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right)\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
If \(d\le n\), the exponential term is at most \(C_{\epsilon}/n\).  If \(n<d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), decreasing \(c_{\epsilon}\), if necessary, makes that term at most \(C_{\epsilon}d/n^2\).  Finally, \((n\vee d)/n^2\le n^{-1}+d/n^2\).  Substitution in \((6)\), followed by clipping, proves the displayed bound.  Conditional moments are invoked only for positive-mass cells, and all empirical division boundaries have the stipulated zero fallback.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exists \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that the following holds.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), let \(V:=Y/M\), \(s_{ak}:=P(X=k,A=a)\), and \(z_{ak}:=E_P[V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]\), and consider a block of \(m\) independent observations with joint law \(Q_P^{(m)}\).  For integers \(K\ge2\), numbers \(B>0\), and
\[
 g_{Kj}:=(-1)^j\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4},\qquad 0\le j\le K-2,
\]
define the ordered, distinct-index statistic
\[
 U_{k,a,j}:=\frac{1}{(m)_{j+2}}
 \sum_{i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1}\ {\rm distinct}}
 V_{i_0}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_0}=k,A_{i_0}=a\}
 \mathbf 1\{X_{i_1}=k\}
 \prod_{t=2}^{j+1}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_t}=k,A_{i_t}=a\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat P_k:=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}\frac{g_{Kj}}{B^{j+1}}
 \{U_{k,1,j}-U_{k,0,j}\}.
\]
If \(S\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B/4\}\) is deterministic, \(4(K+2)^2\le m\), and \(4(K+2)/m\le3B/4\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Q_P^{(m)}}\!\left(\sum_{k\in S}\widehat P_k\right)
 \le \frac{C_{\epsilon}}m+C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}
 \left\{dB^2+\frac{d^2K^2B^2}{m}\right\}.
\]
No boundedness of \(Y\) is required.
statements.justification: This isolates the only new weak-moment covariance step in the continuous-outcome polynomial lift.
statements.gap: Unlike a bounded binary mark, a real mark can overlap itself; the displayed second-moment calculation controls exactly that case.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), put \(\nu_{ak}:=\mu_{ak}/M\), and recall \(V=Y/M\).  Mean normalization gives \(|\nu_{ak}|\le1/2\), while the conditional second-central-moment assumption gives
\[
 E[(V-\nu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le1.
\]
Consequently
\[
 E[V^2\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]
 =s_{ak}\{\operatorname{Var}(V\mid A=a,X=k)+\nu_{ak}^2\}
 \le\frac54s_{ak}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is the only outcome-moment inequality used below.

Every summand defining \(U_{k,a,j}\) contains exactly one marked selector \(V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}\); all other factors are indicators.  Independence of distinct sample indices gives
\[
 E[U_{k,a,j}]=z_{ak}p_ks_{ak}^{j}.
\tag{2}
\]
To calculate a covariance, multiply the two ordered sums defining \(U_{k,a,j}\) and \(U_{\ell,b,r}\) and partition their terms by the partial matching of their index tuples.  A matching of size \(h\) leaves \(j+r+4-h\) distinct observations.  Since \(j+2,r+2\le K\) and \(4K^2\le m\), cancellation of falling factorials yields
\[
 \frac{(m)_{j+r+4-h}}{(m)_{j+2}(m)_{r+2}}
 \le\frac e{m^h},
\tag{3}
\]
and the number of size-\(h\) matchings is at most \(K^{2h}/h!\).

This partition also verifies the moment audit.  If the two marked positions are not identified, each surviving observation carries at most one mark and factors by independence.  If a marked position is matched to an unmarked selector, the expectation is \(z_{ak}\), or zero when the selectors are incompatible, and \(|z_{ak}|\le s_{ak}/2\).  The two marked positions can be identified only when \(k=\ell\) and \(a=b\); that observation then contributes exactly \(E[V^2\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]\), bounded by \((1)\).  Thus no term contains more than two coincident marks.

Define
\[
 G_K(x):=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}g_{Kj}x^j,
 \qquad G_K^+(x):=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}|g_{Kj}|x^j=G_K(-x).
\]
The shifted-Chebyshev identity gives
\[
 G_K^+(x)=\frac{T_K(1+2x)-1-2K^2x}{2K^2x^2},
\]
with the continuous value at zero, and the closed form for \(T_K(t)\) on \(t\ge1\) implies
\[
 G_K^+(x)\le6^K\max\{1,x^{K-2}\},\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(p_k\le B/4\) on \(S\) and \(4(K+2)/m\le3B/4\), every intensity argument produced by a matching in \((3)\) is at most \(B\).  Summing absolute overlap contributions with \((4)\) gives three classes.  A matching that identifies the marked positions is bounded by \(C_{\epsilon}/m\) using \((1)\), overlap, and \(\sum_{k,a}s_{ak}=1\).  The remaining within-cell matchings are bounded by \(C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}dB^2\).  For different cells no cross-tuple index can be shared; after subtracting the product of expectations, only the fixed-sample falling-factorial correction remains, and
\[
 \left|\frac{(m)_{j+r+4}}{(m)_{j+2}(m)_{r+2}}-1\right|
 \le\frac{2K^2}{m}.
\tag{5}
\]
Its total is at most \(C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}d^2K^2B^2/m\).  Adding the three classes proves the displayed variance inequality.  The proof uses only \((1)\), hence only the conditional second-central-moment envelope; boundedness of \(Y\) is nowhere invoked.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon},\rho_{\epsilon}>0\) and a finite \(N_{\epsilon}\) for which the following explicit total estimator is defined.  Put \(L=\log(en)\), split the sample into \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\}\) and its complement \(I_1\), and write \(m_j=|I_j|\).  Set
\[
 \lambda_0=256,\quad b_0=4096,\quad D_6=8\log(27/4),\quad
 \alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{64\log6},\frac1{512D_6}\right\}.
\]
When \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le\rho_{\epsilon}nL\), set \(K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\ge2\), \(B=b_0L/m_1\), classify
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal H}:=\left\{k:\sum_{i\in I_0}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}>\lambda_0L\right\},
 \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}:=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\]
use the statistics \(\widehat P_k\) of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:linear\text{-}mark\text{-}factorial\text{-}covariance}\) on block \(I_1\), and put
\[
 \widehat h_k:=\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\left\{
 \frac{\sum_{i\in I_1}V_i\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=1\}}{N_{1k}^{(1)}}\mathbf 1\{N_{1k}^{(1)}>0\}
 -\frac{\sum_{i\in I_1}V_i\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=0\}}{N_{0k}^{(1)}}\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}^{(1)}>0\}
 \right\}.
\]
Define
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}:=M\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\!\left(
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\widehat h_k+
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k\right).
\]
When \(n<N_{\epsilon}\) or \(d>\rho_{\epsilon}nL\), set \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}=0\).  Then, for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and every \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
The estimator uses \(O(dK^2)\) arithmetic operations after cell aggregation and has bounded fallbacks on every division boundary.
statements.justification: The explicit estimator closes the unrestricted effective-sample-enlargement upper branch for real outcomes.
statements.gap: The proof supplies the marked factorial covariance and fixed-sample calibration absent from the construction handle.
statements.consumer: The robust upper-construction answer and the selector theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  Normalize the outcome and the arm means by
\[
 V:=Y/M,\qquad \nu_{ak}:=\mu_{ak}/M,
\]
and put
\[
 s_{ak}:=P(X=k,A=a),\qquad
 z_{ak}:=E_P[V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}],\qquad
 \varphi_k:=p_k(\nu_{1k}-\nu_{0k}).
\]
For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), define the block counts
\[
 N_k^{(j)}:=\sum_{i\in I_j}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\},
 \qquad
 N_{ak}^{(j)}:=\sum_{i\in I_j}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}.
\]
Definition~\(\mathrm{def:ate\text{-}functional}\), mean normalization, and overlap give
\[
 \frac{\tau(P)}M=\sum_{k=1}^d\varphi_k,\qquad
 z_{ak}=s_{ak}\nu_{ak},\qquad
 |\nu_{ak}|\le\frac12,\qquad
 s_{ak}\ge\epsilon p_k.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(V\mid A=a,X=k)\le1.
\tag{2}
\]
This is the only tail control used below.

Let \(T_K\) be the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind and, with continuous extensions at zero, define
\[
 H_K(x):=\frac{1-T_K(1-2x)}{2K^2},\qquad
 E_K(x):=\frac{H_K(x)}x,\qquad
 G_K(x):=\frac{1-E_K(x)}x.
\]
Expanding the shifted Chebyshev polynomial gives
\[
 G_K(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}(-1)^j
 \frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4}x^j
 =\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}g_{Kj}x^j.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(0\le x\le1\), write \(1-2x=\cos\theta\).  The identity \(T_K(\cos\theta)=\cos(K\theta)\) implies \(|T_K(1-2x)|\le1\), and therefore
\[
 0\le x\{1-xG_K(x)\}=H_K(x)\le K^{-2}.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(p_k\le B\), equations~\((1)\) and \((4)\), with \(x=s_{ak}/B\in[0,1]\), imply
\[
 \left|p_k\nu_{ak}-\frac{p_kz_{ak}}B G_K(s_{ak}/B)\right|
 =p_k|\nu_{ak}|\,|1-xG_K(x)|
 \le\frac{B}{2\epsilon K^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Independence of the ordered distinct indices in \(U_{k,a,j}\) gives
\[
 E_P[U_{k,a,j}]=z_{ak}p_ks_{ak}^{j}.
\]
Consequently \(\widehat P_k\) is unbiased for
\[
 \frac{p_kz_{1k}}B G_K(s_{1k}/B)-
 \frac{p_kz_{0k}}B G_K(s_{0k}/B).
\tag{6}
\]

For the independent pilot block put
\[
 B_-:=\frac{\lambda_0L}{2m_0},\qquad
 B_+:=\frac{2\lambda_0L}{m_0},
\]
and define the event
\[
 \mathcal A:=\left\{
 \widehat{\mathcal H}\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\},\quad
 \widehat{\mathcal L}\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
 \right\}.
\]
The balanced split and \(b_0=16\lambda_0\) imply \(B_+\le B/4\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  For completeness, if \(D\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(t,q)\), exponential Markov applied to \(E[e^{uD}]=(1-q+qe^u)^t\) at \(u=\log2\) and \(u=-\log2\) gives
\[
 P(D\ge2tq)\le(e/4)^{tq},
 \qquad
 P(D\le tq/2)\le e^{-tq/8}.
\]
Applying these inequalities on the two sides of the pilot threshold and taking a union bound over the \(d\) cells yields
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(\mathcal A^c)
 \le2d\exp(-c\lambda_0L)
 \le Cn^{-6}
\tag{7}
\]
uniformly for \(d\le\rho_{\epsilon}nL\), after decreasing \(\rho_{\epsilon}\) if necessary.

Condition on the pilot block and suppose \(\mathcal A\) occurs.  Then the light set is deterministic relative to \(I_1\) and is contained in \(\{k:p_k\le B/4\}\).  Since \(K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\), \(B=b_0L/m_1\), and \(\alpha_0,b_0\) are the displayed fixed constants, increasing \(N_{\epsilon}\) ensures
\[
 K\ge2,\qquad 4(K+2)^2\le m_1,\qquad
 \frac{4(K+2)}{m_1}\le\frac{3B}{4}.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations~\((5)\)--\((6)\) and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:linear\text{-}mark\text{-}factorial\text{-}covariance}\) therefore give
\[
\begin{split}
 E_P\left[\left\{
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\varphi_k
 \right\}^2\middle|I_0\right]
 \le C_{\epsilon}\left[
 \frac1{m_1}+6^{2K}\left\{dB^2+
 \frac{d^2K^2B^2}{m_1}\right\}
 +\frac{d^2B^2}{K^4}
 \right].
\end{split}
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, the final term is the square of the sum of the cellwise biases in \((5)\), and the other terms are precisely the covariance lemma's variance bound.

Let \(\kappa:=2\alpha_0\log6\le1/32\).  Since \(6^{2K}\le n^\kappa\), \(B\le CL/n\), and \(K\le CL\), elementary completion of squares gives, uniformly in \(d\ge1\),
\[
 n^\kappa\frac{dL^2}{n^2}
 \le C\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 n^\kappa\frac{d^2L^4}{n^3}
 \le C\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}.
\tag{10}
\]
Also \(dB/K^2\le Cd/(nL)\).  Substitution in \((9)\) proves
\[
 E_P\left[\left\{
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\varphi_k
 \right\}^2\middle|I_0\right]
 \le C_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac1n+
 \frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]

We next treat the heavy cells.  Conditional on the pilot and on the category and treatment indicators in \(I_1\), equation~\((2)\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\left(
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\widehat h_k
 \middle|(X_i,A_i)_{i\in I_1}\right)
 \le\frac1{m_1^2}\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}(N_k^{(1)})^2
 \left\{
 \frac{\mathbf1\{N_{1k}^{(1)}>0\}}{N_{1k}^{(1)}}+
 \frac{\mathbf1\{N_{0k}^{(1)}>0\}}{N_{0k}^{(1)}}
 \right\}.
\tag{12}
\]
For \(D\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(t,q)\), integration of \(E[x^D]=(1-q+qx)^t\) over \([0,1]\) gives
\[
 E[(D+1)^{-1}]=\frac{1-(1-q)^{t+1}}{(t+1)q}.
\]
Together with \(D^{-1}\mathbf1\{D>0\}\le2(D+1)^{-1}\), overlap, and conditioning first on \(N_k^{(1)}\), this shows that the expectation of the right side of \((12)\) is at most \(C_{\epsilon}/m_1\).

The conditional outcome mean of the heavy sum is
\[
 \frac1{m_1}\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}N_k^{(1)}
 (\nu_{1k}-\nu_{0k})-R_1+R_0,
\]
where
\[
 R_a:=\frac1{m_1}\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}
 N_k^{(1)}\nu_{ak}\mathbf1\{N_{ak}^{(1)}=0\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Conditional on the pilot, the first term is an empirical average of a function bounded in absolute value by one; it is unbiased for \(\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\varphi_k\) and has variance at most \(1/m_1\).  Exact multinomial factorial moments, \(|\nu_{ak}|\le1/2\), and \(s_{ak}\ge\epsilon p_k\) give
\[
 E_P[R_a^2\mid I_0]
 \le C_{\epsilon}\left[
 \frac1{m_1}+
 \left\{\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}
 p_ke^{-c_{\epsilon}m_1p_k}\right\}^2
 \right].
\tag{14}
\]
On \(\mathcal A\), every selected heavy cell has \(p_k\ge B_-\ge cL/n\).  Hence \(p_ke^{-c_{\epsilon}m_1p_k}\le C_{\epsilon}/(nL)\) after increasing \(N_{\epsilon}\), and
\[
 E_P[R_a^2\mid I_0]
 \le C_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac1n+
 \frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Combining \((12)\)--\((15)\) proves the heavy-cell analogue of \((11)\).

The selected heavy and light sets partition all cells.  Let \(Z\) denote the normalized sum before clipping.  The heavy and light bounds, equation~\((1)\), and \((x+y)^2\le2x^2+2y^2\) yield
\[
 E_P\left[\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}
 \left\{Z-\frac{\tau(P)}M\right\}^2\right]
 \le C_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac1n+
 \frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}.
\tag{16}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scale\text{-}sanity}\) gives \(\tau(P)/M\in[-1,1]\).  Projection onto \([-1,1]\) therefore cannot increase squared loss, and the projected squared loss is at most four on \(\mathcal A^c\).  Equations~\((7)\) and \((16)\) prove the asserted rate when \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le\rho_{\epsilon}nL\).

If \(d>\rho_{\epsilon}nL\), the zero fallback has loss at most \(M^2\), while
\[
 \min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}\right\}
 \ge\min\{1,\rho_{\epsilon}^2\}.
\]
If \(n<N_{\epsilon}\), the same conclusion follows from \(1\le N_{\epsilon}/n\).  Enlarging \(C_{\epsilon}\) proves the displayed risk inequality throughout \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\).

All sample-mean ratios are multiplied by positive-denominator indicators.  Moreover, after cell aggregation, the unnormalized ordered sum in \(U_{k,a,j}\) equals
\[
 \left(\sum_{i\in I_1}V_i\mathbf1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\right)
 (N_{ak}^{(1)}-1)_j(N_k^{(1)}-j-1),
\]
with value zero whenever there are too few distinct indices.  Thus the estimator is measurable and total.  Computing all coefficients and factorial terms takes \(O(dK^2)\) arithmetic operations, and no boundary division is left undefined.

Finally, equations~\((1)\)--\((2)\) imply for every law in the note's real-outcome class that
\[
 E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]
 =\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid A=a,X=k)+\mu_{ak}^2
 \le M^2+\frac{M^2}{4}=\frac{5M^2}{4}.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus the broader formal outcome support does not itself supply a novelty claim relative to the weak-second-moment rate-valid envelope stated by Zeng--Balakrishnan--Han--Kennedy.  The construction-level increment proved here is the explicit fixed-sample signed one-mark Chebyshev/factorial estimator, together with the covariance control that avoids an extra logarithmic loss; downstream it is paired with the collision estimator in the known-radius selector and converse comparison.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) denote the binary-outcome class with arbitrary cell masses, fixed overlap \(\epsilon\), consistency, conditional exchangeability, and arm means in \([0,1]\), and let \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be its uniform-mass, exactly homogeneous subclass.  The affine map
\[
 \Phi_M:\quad B(a)\longmapsto Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y=Y(A),
\]
embeds \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), and embeds \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,0}\subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  The image is a strict subclass of the note's real-outcome class.  Restriction to the image of \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) transfers the lower term \(M^2(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\), while applying the hypothesis-independent channel in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) to the binary one-arm hard family transfers the radius term
\[
 M^2\sigma^2\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
Thus the lower bounds arise by subclass restriction, whereas the explicit signed-mark upper estimator is proved on the broader real-outcome class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).
statements.justification: This proposition makes the published binary subclasses and every converse transfer explicit while separating them from the broader-class upper theorem.
statements.gap: The anchor anticipates moment-bounded extensions, so real outcomes alone are not positioned as novel; it does not provide this note's fixed-sample signed-mark estimator.
statements.consumer: The proposition audits exactly which lower bounds transfer by subclass restriction and why the upper construction applies beyond those subclasses.
statements.proof_tex:
Take a source law in \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\).  If only its observed conditional Bernoulli distributions are specified, augment it by drawing \(B(0),B(1)\) conditionally on \(X\), independently of \(A\), with the prescribed arm means.  This leaves the observed experiment unchanged and makes consistency and conditional exchangeability explicit.  Define
\[
 Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y:=Y(A).
\tag{1}
\]
The cell masses and propensities are unchanged, so overlap is preserved.  If
\(
 \eta_{ak}:=E[B\mid A=a,X=k]
\), then
\[
 \mu_{ak}=M(\eta_{ak}-1/2)\in[-M/2,M/2].
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, \(|Y-\mu_{ak}|=M|B-\eta_{ak}|\le M\), and hence
\[
 E[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations~\((1)\)--\((3)\), together with consistency, conditional exchangeability, and overlap, prove that every source law maps into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).

The cell effects and the ATE are scaled by \(M\):
\[
 \tau_k=M(\eta_{1k}-\eta_{0k}),
 \qquad
 \tau(P)=M\sum_{k=1}^dp_k(\eta_{1k}-\eta_{0k}).
\tag{4}
\]
Therefore exact homogeneity of a uniform-mass source law is preserved.  Thus \(\Phi_M\) maps \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,0}\), which is contained in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for each \(0\le\sigma\le2\).

The formal inclusion is strict.  Put all mass on \(X=1\), let \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and, independently of \(A\), let \(Z_0,Z_1\) be independent and uniform on \(\{-M/4,0,M/4\}\).  Set \(Y(a)=Z_a\) and \(Y=Y(A)\).  The arm means and all treatment effects vanish, while
\[
 E[Z_a^2]=\frac{M^2}{24}\le M^2.
\tag{5}
\]
This law satisfies consistency, conditional exchangeability, overlap, mean normalization, the second-central-moment bound, and approximate homogeneity at every radius.  It is not in the affine binary image because each conditional outcome law has three support points, whereas every image law is supported on \(\{-M/2,M/2\}\).  Hence the image is a strict subclass of the note's formal real-outcome class.

On the exactly homogeneous image, the observed transformation \(B=Y/M+1/2\) is invertible and squared ATE error is multiplied by \(M^2\).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:scaled\text{-}binary\text{-}exact\text{-}lower\text{-}transfer}\) therefore transfers the lower term
\[
 M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\tag{6}
\]
For the one-arm family, the hypothesis-independent channel in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) preserves total-variation control by data processing and transfers
\[
 M^2\sigma^2\min\left\{1,
 \frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
\tag{7}
\]
up to constants depending only on \(\epsilon\).  Both lower bounds are therefore obtained by restricting the note's supremum to scaled binary subclasses.

By contrast, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) proves its signed-mark estimator uniformly on \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  Every law in that class satisfies
\[
 E[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]
 =\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=a,X=k)+\mu_{ak}^2
 \le\frac{5M^2}{4}.
\tag{8}
\]
The anchor's formal model is binary, but the anchor also states that its rates remain valid under a uniform weak-second-moment envelope of this kind.  Accordingly, the three-point example witnesses strict inclusion only at the level of the formal classes; it is not a novelty claim based on allowing real outcomes.  The theorem-level increment is instead the explicit fixed-sample signed one-mark Chebyshev/factorial construction, its covariance proof without an extra logarithmic loss, and its downstream combination with the collision estimator in the known-radius selector and converse comparison.

statements.statement:
In the binary-outcome model of Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, let \(\psi:=\sum_{k=1}^dp_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\), let \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}:=\max_{1\le k\le d}|\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}-\psi|\), and let \(\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{col}}\) be their occupancy-weighted estimator in equation (13).  Under overlap \(\epsilon\), their Theorem 3 states
\[
 |E(\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{col}}-\psi)|
 \le \sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}+2\exp\left\{-C(\epsilon)\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{col}})
 \lesssim_{\epsilon}\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}^2+\frac d{n^2}+\frac1n.
\]

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
 \le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
Both inequalities hold on the same real-outcome, arbitrary-cell-mass class.  This is a two-sided minimax bracket, not a claim that the two displayed benchmarks are uniformly order-equivalent at every shrinking interior radius.

The accepted-bank theorem \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior} establishes the unrestricted binary-outcome hybrid rate \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\).  The present theorem is not a restatement of that endpoint: on one arbitrary-cell-mass real-outcome class under conditional-second-central-moment control, it gives a known-radius upper and lower minimax bracket.  Its increment is the radius-indexed same-class bracket, the explicit weak-moment signed-mark construction and known-radius selector, the radius-channel converse, and the localization of every remaining possible mismatch to the explicit shrinking-radius wedge in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:fixed\text{-}interior\text{-}tightness\text{-}and\text{-}shrinking\text{-}radius\text{-}gap}\); real outcomes alone are not claimed as novel.
statements.justification: This is the honest all-radius same-class minimax conclusion: a proved bracket whose matched regimes are stated separately.
statements.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy provide the binary endpoint bounds and collision upper branch but leave uniform radius dependence open; the present converse does not close the shrinking-radius triangular regime.
statements.consumer: A downstream reader can use the upper benchmark for estimator choice and the lower benchmark for impossibility claims without treating the remaining logarithmic gap as solved.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\), \(\kappa_{\epsilon}\in(0,1)\), \(c_{\epsilon}>0\), and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that the explicit estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{ctr}}\) of Definition~\(\mathrm{def:centered\text{-}product\text{-}estimator}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\) and, uniformly for \(0\le\sigma\le2\), \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\), \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), and
\[
 u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\le\kappa_{\epsilon},
\]
satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2u
 \right\}.
\]
The construction is clipped and total and requires no outcome tail condition beyond Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\).

Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  There are constants \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\), \(\rho_{\epsilon}>0\), and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that the following holds.  Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), use a block of \(m\ge N_{\epsilon}\) observations, put \(L_m:=\log(em)\), \(K:=\lfloor\alpha L_m\rfloor\), and \(B:=\beta_{\epsilon}L_m/m\), with \(\alpha\) and \(\beta_{\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:centered\text{-}product\text{-}estimator}\).  Write \(V:=Y/M\), \(\vartheta:=\tau(P)/M\), \(\vartheta_k:=\tau_k/M\), \(s_{ak}:=P(X=k,A=a)\), and \(z_{ak}:=E_P[V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]\).  For deterministic \(S\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B/4\}\), fixed \(t\in[-1,1]\), and the signed mixed-arm statistics \(\widehat P_k(t)\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:centered\text{-}product\text{-}estimator}\), if \(d\le\rho_{\epsilon}mL_m\), then
\[
 E[\widehat P_k(t)]
 =H_k(t)\{r_{K,B}(s_{0k})+r_{K,B}(s_{1k})\},
 \qquad
 H_k(t):=s_{0k}s_{1k}(\vartheta_k-t),
\]
where \(r_{K,B}(s):=B^{-1}G_K(s/B)\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{k\in S}\widehat P_k(t)\right)
 \le C_{\epsilon}\left\{
 \frac1m+\frac d{m^2}
 +\frac{d^2}{m^2L_m^2}
 \bigl[\sigma^2+(t-\vartheta)^2\bigr]
 \right\}.
\]
The inequality uses only the conditional-second-central-moment envelope; it does not require bounded outcomes.

For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, uniformly for \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the explicit total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) in the corrected Definition~\(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma},
\]
where
\[
 r_{n,d,\sigma}:=\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}
 +\sigma^2\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
Relative to the collision guarantee of Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, the radius contribution is multiplied by \(\min\{1,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\); the bound is on the same arbitrary-cell-mass real-outcome class under the conditional-second-central-moment envelope.

Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\), and \(s:=\sigma^2\).  Uniformly on the range of Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:sharp\text{-}two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax}\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \asymp_{\epsilon}M^2\{b+s\min(1,u)\}.
\]
Consequently: exact homogeneity has rate \(M^2b\); unrestricted heterogeneity \((\sigma=2)\) has rate \(M^2\{b+\min(1,u)\}\); every fixed positive radius has rate \(M^2\{b+\min(1,u)\}\); saturation \(u\ge1\) has rate \(M^2(b+s)\); and either \(u\lesssim b\) or \(s\min(1,u)\lesssim b\) yields the parametric-dominance rate \(M^2b\).  In the formerly residual wedge \(b\ll u\ll1\) and \(b\ll s\ll1\), the sharp rate is \(M^2(b+su)\).  For \(d_n=n\) and \(\sigma_n=\log(en)^{-1/2}\), it is of order \(M^2\log(en)^{-3}\), improving the former selector benchmark by a factor of order \(\log(en)\).  No shrinking-radius regime remains unresolved at the level of minimax mean-squared-error order.

The shrinking-radius question has an affirmative estimator-side answer.  The explicit centered mixed-arm factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{ctr}}\), using an independent clipped occupancy pilot and the signed kernel in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:centered\text{-}product\text{-}estimator}\), satisfies throughout \(u\le\kappa_{\epsilon}\)
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\{b+\sigma^2u\}.
\]
Combined with the occupancy branch for \(u>\kappa_{\epsilon}\) and the radius-channel converse, this yields the uniform sharp minimax rate \(M^2\{b+\sigma^2\min(1,u)\}\).  In particular, the earlier residual wedge is resolved without a stronger fuzzy experiment.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling under the induced product law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\), with the one-unit full-data law \(P\) satisfying consistency and conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), independently distributed with common law \(P_O\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with fixed strong overlap \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass cell.
sampling_model.overlap: The constant \(\epsilon\) is fixed; the cell masses \(p_k\) are arbitrary and unknown.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensity, two outcome regressions, and cell masses are unknown; the total selector combines robust heavy-light polynomial and same-cell collision estimators using known \(M\) and \(\sigma\).

estimand_functional:
With \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), and \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\{b+\sigma^2\min(1,u)\}
 \le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\{n^{-1}+\min(1,u,\sigma^2+d/n^2)\}.
\]
Both inequalities range over the arbitrary-cell-mass real-outcome model with conditional means in \([-M/2,M/2]\) and conditional second central moments bounded by \(M^2\).  The benchmarks are order-equivalent at fixed positive radii and whenever \(u\ge1\), \(u\lesssim b\), or \(\sigma^2\lesssim b\); only \(b\ll u\ll1\), \(b\ll\sigma^2\ll1\) remains potentially divergent

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (12) on page 10 and Theorem 3 on page 11 bound the binary-outcome collision estimator by the maximal heterogeneity term plus \(d/n^2+1/n\); the model discussion also states that the paper's rates remain valid whenever \(E[Y^2\mid X=k,A=a]\le C\).
Theorem 3 gives the exact-homogeneity collision upper rate, and Theorem 4 on page 12 gives the matching lower bound on the uniform-mass subclass \(\mathcal H(\epsilon)\).
Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 gives the unrestricted binary-outcome lower scale \(d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]+1/n\) in its stated range.
The nonsmooth branch evaluates a best polynomial approximation with unbiased factorial-moment estimators, while the smooth branch uses a bias-corrected plug-in estimator.
Best-polynomial upper constructions and moment-matching lower priors are dual tools for large-alphabet minimax estimation.

A multivariate median construction attains sub-Gaussian mean performance under finite second moments; that construction is not used here, where signed one-mark factorial statistics and final clipping suffice for mean-squared-error control.

The accepted-bank theorem establishes the unrestricted arbitrary-cell-mass binary-outcome hybrid rate \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\).  The present theorem does not claim novelty merely from real outcomes; its increment is the radius-indexed same-class bracket, explicit weak-moment signed-mark construction and known-radius selector, radius-channel converse, and localization of every remaining possible mismatch to the shrinking-radius wedge.

tldr: High-dimensional discrete adjustment has two complementary information sources: a signed-mark heavy--light polynomial estimator handles rare cells, while an occupancy-weighted treated--control estimator exploits nearly common cell effects. Under fixed overlap, arbitrary unknown cell masses, real outcomes with conditional means in \([-M/2,M/2]\), a uniform conditional second central moment bounded by \(M^2\), and maximal cell-effect deviation at most \(\sigma M\), an explicit known-radius selector attains \(C_{\epsilon}M^2\{n^{-1}+\min[1,d^2/(n^2\log^2(en)),\sigma^2+d/n^2]\}\). A same-class converse gives \(c_{\epsilon}M^2\{n^{-1}+d/n^2+\sigma^2\min[1,d^2/(n^2\log^2(en))]\}\). The benchmarks match at both endpoints, every fixed positive radius, saturation, and both parametric-dominance elbows; only the localized shrinking-radius wedge remains potentially divergent. The scale normalization makes \(\sigma=2\) exactly unrestricted. No inference or adaptation to unknown \(M\) or \(\sigma\) is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy give the unrestricted lower bound in Theorem 2, the approximate-homogeneity upper bound in Theorem 3, and the exact-homogeneity uniform-mass lower bound in Theorem 4; Section 4.2 on page 12 explicitly leaves sharp minimax dependence on the maximal heterogeneity radius open.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a three-branch phase diagram in which collision information controls small radii, the radius itself is the bottleneck in the middle, and large-alphabet polynomial smoothing takes over before heterogeneity is unrestricted.
project_justification.fill: The project defines a total known-radius selector from robust polynomial and collision inputs, derives the exact collision target and corrected scale endpoint, and seeks one same-class radius-indexed converse matching all three branches for continuous outcomes.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy study the same discrete observational structure for binary outcomes. Their equation (12) on page 10 and Theorem 3 on page 11 give the approximate-homogeneity collision upper branch; Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 gives the unrestricted lower branch; Theorem 4 and Section 4.2 on page 12 give the exact-homogeneity uniform-mass lower bound and state that sharp radius dependence remains open. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman provide the heavy-light architecture based on best-polynomial approximation and factorial-moment lifting. Wu and Yang connect polynomial upper constructions to moment-matching lower priors. Hoeffding supplies the order-two projection decomposition relevant to collision statistics. Lugosi and Mendelson motivate weak-moment robust aggregation but do not supply the conditional moment assumptions or the marked factorial construction used here. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman derive a causal minimax interpolation for smooth heterogeneous-effect estimation, not for a growing discrete alphabet or maximal effect homogeneity.
technical_internal_limitation: The proposal does not claim inference, adaptation to unknown \(M\) or \(\sigma\), sharp constants, or a preferred finite-sample tuning. The mean interval is a normalization that preserves the requested \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) endpoint; replacing it by \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) would enlarge the automatically unrestricted radius to four and would change the headline parameterization.
honest_scope: Identification, the collision expectation identity, and the endpoint algebra are settled targets for verification. The open mathematical content is the weak-moment no-extra-log construction and the same-class radius-indexed fuzzy-hypothesis converse. The proof program does not address deteriorating overlap, latent effect groups, inference, or adaptation to unknown scale or radius.
